tasks.title: Execute many independent SQLite cells through one real Raft group

steps.action: Split the combined host Cell owner into group consensus state and per-cell execution state. One GroupHistory owns exactly one RawNode per voter; cell count does not allocate additional RawNodes. Reuse shared persistence, transport and SQL pools. Integrate CG-03 enrollment decisions with replicated enrollment and independent SQLite initialization before exposing cell commands. Atomically retain the immutable enrollment creation record with the selected cell state; preserve it through mutations and transfer so retries never reinitialize or restore the initial image over newer state. Consume the prepared CellRoutingSession attempts when integrating dispatch: preserve the logical request fingerprint, original domain deadline and total attempt budget across member retries and group redirects. Catalog-confirmed mappings are hints; destination admission must validate the full binding and current authority. Command producers remain domain-owned after a routing waiter is cancelled.

Admit one unresolved proposal per cell with fair cell queues and group/node byte quotas. Allow independent cells to prepare concurrently, then publish committed entries through one contiguous group prefix with per-cell base/version checks. Enforce configured group enrollment capacity on the actual owner before append, counting applied cells and pending accepted logical creations. Exact creation retries consume no additional slot; competing creations cannot exceed the limit before apply. Verify capacity refusal leaves existing cells available and release reservations only with proven resolution.

Implement exact per-cell output settlement and receipt retry. Group no-ops/configuration entries advance group apply without changing cell version. Reject stale term/activation/completion tickets and preserve unknown proposed outcomes. Check the prepared term atomically with proposal admission on the actual Raft owner. Bind same-term acceptance retries to the original proposal identity and bytes; a lost acceptance response must recover retained acceptance or reconcile the original receipt without appending the same mutation again. Reject changed payloads under a reused identity, and retain uncertainty across elections until an applied barrier proves resolution. A definitive pre-append owner refusal must irreversibly seal all clones of that preparation before returning an identity-bound rejection proof. Generic queue errors cannot retire a submitted SQL producer. Close rejected producers on their owning worker before releasing name admission; delayed retries and proofs from another preparation must not affect a replacement producer.

Implement Stale, AtLeast and current-term ReadIndex for the target cell. Pin coherent manifest/image views and include cross-cell noninterference and slow-apply cases in the real-engine fixture. Correlate each strong read to its own runtime-owned request context and absolute domain deadline; retain separate bounded node/group pin admission through delivery and physical SQL execution. Configure logical image-pin bytes independently of transport message/request bytes; validate overflow and supported image bounds, and test independent capacity and reservation cleanup. Persist each selected version's full commit witness in the authenticated manifest and require exact proposal matching at apply. Keep original decision provenance separate from local installation position, retain it across unchanged-cell progress/restart and carry it through query and receipt observations. Missing witness fields must refuse at marker 1. Query callbacks consume immutable pins on existing workers, preserve read-only SQL policy and contain panics. Deadline/cancellation must interrupt SQLite work while arbitrary callback ownership remains retained until it finishes; shutdown joins that work.

Run physical group apply on the existing node SQL workers with independent bounded progress admission. Transfer the startup manifest-page owner, verify the exact committed entry/base, prepare either cell image representation and derive bounded scheduling summaries. Retain preparation through response cancellation and physical publication. Materialized retries may pin only the exact verified prepared image; they cannot infer publication or reset retirement. Test the physical image store retry across restart and corruption, and reject malformed effect tables rather than reporting idle. Keep membership/topology administrative apply explicitly refused until its owning tasks implement it.

Qualify image and manifest I/O ownership at actual held/failing directory barriers. Recover complete cell-group images through the same stable physical naming and verified extent bindings used by apply; accept only the engine-selected root and retain its exact cell versions/witnesses. Cold restart may replay a committed unpublished entry but never substitutes selected files or inherited commit state for fresh serving authority. Missing closure refuses before owner admission. Keep whole-process kill/power-loss qualification distinct from joined cold restart.

Use logical CellHistory at registered command and signed-effect identity boundaries. Dispatch namespace-authorized classes on the existing shared SQL workers; validate operation, schema, input and authenticated inbox identity before receipt lookup. Preserve exact proposal submission/settlement and cancellation ownership. Group placement is absent from effect identity; fresh cell incarnations remain fenced. Marker-1 old group-bearing effect wire and old signature domains refuse. Catalog/SDK dispatch remains separate integration work.

Dispatch compiled queries through the existing coherent query worker and callback guard with the actual CellVersionObservation, bounded operation/input admission and original read deadline. Keep legacy group cuts explicitly typed during integration; never fabricate a cell sequence or witness. Remove the temporary group-cut observation and old constructor with CG-16; final serving uses the common cell-group path.

Connect catalog routing sessions to compiled query execution with a namespace-bound class and captured input/consistency. Share bounded invocation admission across dispatcher clones, preserve the original domain deadline and total retry budget, consume each attempt before entering asynchronous work, authenticate AtLeast cell tokens and return a token for the selected observation. Exact destination route and engine checks remain mandatory; a confirmed catalog redirect cannot invent a physical owner. Dropping the routing invocation must leave entered SQL owned until joined cleanup. Command/enrollment dispatch and final public SDK replacement remain required.

Route immutable registered command invocations through the same dispatcher and catalog sessions. Capture host time/randomness once, retain the original runtime/SQL producer across cancelled preparation, and resume it before considering a new destination. Submission acceptance is provisional; settle only an exact committed receipt or the existing newer-term absence proof. Preserve command identity, deadline and attempt budget across retries, and refuse S3 requests or S3 namespace minima until a real archive proof is integrated. The production controller must retain active invocations and drive publication; enrollment and the public SDK/controller cutover remain required.

Connect physical group histories to the existing node-owned peer transport without constructing the legacy runtime. Share TLS pools, lanes, byte/item banks, revocation and joined shutdown. Bind typed marker-1 history and full replica identity to authenticated requests/responses; refuse old untagged wire layouts and unsupported group snapshots. Include physical routes in all resource and endpoint-conflict checks. The temporary legacy runtime/frame adapter must be deleted with the old host in CG-16. Qualify actual multi-group replication and routed command settlement over TLS before integrating the production controller.

Own the exclusive shared event stream and bounded per-group apply jobs in one node controller. Preserve exact owner bindings and retain physical tickets through backpressure and joined shutdown. Admit fresh command invocations independently from response waiters; retain bounded ownership beyond disconnect/deadline until exact receipt, proven non-commit or joined shutdown. Seal only never-attempted preparations across all clones. Distinguish completed stage errors from lost worker replies and never automatically replay uncertain callbacks.

Register initialization with an explicit digest in the class voting schema. Route immutable creation IDs and captured host inputs through the existing catalog session into the node controller. Share command/enrollment queues and admission, preserve original response deadlines, seal only never-attempted preparations and resolve the original immutable creation record after commitment or later mutations. Distinguish completed initialization errors from lost replies, join physical shutdown, and refuse unsupported S3 durability. The old public host must refuse registered initialization until its shared-runtime cutover; do not silently ignore the callback.

Route consumed shared query attempts through the existing physical peer query lane. Bind physical history, logical cell, schema, route epoch and birth to the authenticated request; use the same read-only namespace grant/revocation guard as existing queries. Destination catalog and runtime authority remain mandatory. Return signed cell observations while retaining bounded result admission, and preserve original deadlines and attempts across retries/redirects. Cancellation must leave entered SQL physically owned until joined cleanup. Complete nonmember shared discovery and public SDK binding separately; mutation RPC must use explicit write authorization, never query-origin grants. Remove temporary legacy query framing and serving with CG-16. Separate public registration admission lifetime from data retained by accepted queries; the last host registration drop must refuse new requests even while an earlier callback is held. Assign query wire sequence numbers in the single peer sender after dequeueing so concurrent ingress cannot cause a false replay refusal.

Install bounded physical read discovery for nonmember routers without creating a local group or borrowing voting authority. Include it in shared peer-pool lifetime, endpoint consistency, node-process refresh and route admission/observability. Revalidate captured route identity before sending and after receiving. Destination namespace grants remain independently authenticated, revocable and strictly read-only. Qualify absent, foreign-namespace and wrong-process grants and held-callback revocation over real TLS, preserving physical SQL ownership. Integrate trusted discovery publication and selection into the public host in CG-07; this API does not authorize automatic membership or mutation RPC.

Share bounded namespace range hints across query, command and enrollment invocations, with explicit entry/byte reservations and LRU eviction. Cache ranges rather than cells; a failed metadata refresh does not invent a new serving proof. Verified successor heads invalidate prior hints and older in-flight observations cannot refill them. Preserve fresh destination RPC admission until replicated transfer-seal authority is integrated. Run the full native_cell_groups_catalog suite, including dispatcher_route_cache_shares_ranges_across_operations, dispatcher_route_cache_bounds_and_refreshes_hints and dispatcher_route_cache_refuses_superseded_inflight_refill, alongside the real runtime case below. Cached mappings never replace runtime ownership, exact cell/version checks, current-term quorum or producer ownership.

Connect remote shared commands to the existing bounded RPC lane and controller. Authenticate command purpose separately from read payloads, require independent bounded namespace/process write grants even for voters, and include those grants in endpoint consistency, process refresh, fleet revocation and pool lifecycle. Preserve captured inputs, immutable command identity, remaining timeout and attempt budget. Destination fresh catalog binding precedes actual leader/SQL authority; only committed exact receipts and signed cell observations return success. Disconnect/revocation cannot cancel already admitted ownership. Also run all query_wire tests, including shared_command_wire_preserves_inputs_and_refuses_query_payloads, shared_command_purpose_is_authenticated_and_cannot_reuse_read_reply and shared_command_results_bind_identity_history_and_typed_refusals. Remote enrollment and standalone receipt lookup are specified in later steps. Run command_grants_bound_tombstones_without_changing_read_permission in the full transport suite to qualify independent read grants, write tombstone caps and shared-pool cleanup. Distinguish follower execution-authority requests as NotLeader from leaders awaiting durable apply (NotReady); preserve stale captured-authority checks.

Route enrollment through the same bounded write RPC exchange, explicit namespace/process grants and exact controller registration as commands. Authenticate Query, Command and Enrollment as distinct mandatory purposes under marker 1, with no legacy reader. Preserve creation identity, captured inputs, preview identity and original routing budget. Recheck fresh destination catalog and leader authority before transferring initialization to the controller; return only the exact committed creation record, never treat the initial image as a current version token. Reuse shared reply budgets and preserve ownership after response disconnect, revocation and publication deadline. Run all query_wire tests including shared_enrollment_wire_preserves_captured_identity_and_inputs, shared_enrollment_purpose_cannot_be_reinterpreted_as_command_or_read and shared_enrollment_reply_binds_creation_cell_schema_and_initial_image, plus all existing command/query and controller enrollment regressions. Standalone receipt lookup follows below; dynamic roster and public SDK cutover remain open.

Add standalone local and remote receipt inspection with a distinct authenticated purpose on the bounded existing RPC exchange. Require explicit command-origin permission and exact controller/SQL ownership; validate command contract, payload digest and authenticated identity before reading receipts. Select a fresh catalog-bound quorum image and use immutable SQL without staging a producer, installing schema, maintaining receipts, or invoking a command/initializer. Return exact retained result/identity and signed cell observation, or ambiguous absence; absence must never retire an unresolved producer. Reuse physical read cancellation, deadline, byte accounting and joined cleanup. Run full query_wire and receipts suites, including shared_receipt_wire_refuses_command_payloads_and_preserves_identity, shared_receipt_reply_distinguishes_unknown_from_empty_committed_result, shared_receipt_purpose_cannot_authorize_mutation and cell_lookup_distinguishes_initial_absence_from_lost_schema. Keep corrupt/partial schema and replicated expiry distinct from absence. Dynamic roster/lazy group birth, per-group failure isolation, configuration lifecycle and public SDK cutover remain incomplete.

Replace the fixed controller roster with bounded dynamic registration, including empty-controller startup. Reserve pending plus active group slots and shared command item/byte admission before transfer. Bind exact engine/history/schema, selected root and applier page owner; install an exclusively owned physical route without adopting a prior registration. Register the applier before polling attachment so early consensus/apply events remain owned. Revalidate the bootstrap catalog through the existing runtime attach path; expose application roster membership only after success, with fresh quorum still required. Retain attachment through response cancellation and join catalog/runtime attachment before closing physical dependencies. Release definite failures before responding; unexpected competing runtime owners or runtime closure keep the conservative node shutdown boundary. Complete-group membership changes follow CG-05; production request/voter orchestration and SDK/fleet binding follow CG-07. Run the full transport and shared runtime suites.

Isolate group-local controller apply/runtime/ambiguous command failures through a bounded retained quarantine lifecycle. Reserve a control lane to revoke execution while apply is waiting, refuse new group admission, preserve captured producer/apply owners until joined shutdown, and prevent late persistence completion from restoring authority. Keep failed group capacity charged. Shared engine I/O/corruption/closure and lost shared SQL worker replies still close the node. Expose original group failure and quarantine counts; no in-place replacement or automatic callback replay. Qualify healthy-group SQL progress and node-wide storage failure separately. Explicit local provisioning uses the lifecycle below; production configuration and public cutover are integrated in CG-07 and CG-16.

Provision already selected initial-member ranges through the controller with immutable explicit filesystem/image/peer settings. Bound preparation bytes, parallelism, resident failed preparations and response waiters independently from commands. Coalesce by exact physical group and directory owner; preserve recovered page owners across attachment retries. Register appliers before polling attachment and join entered catalog/filesystem work before physical shutdown. This explicit local API does not allocate ranges, orchestrate followers, authorize managed fleet admission or wire automatic request-driven/public SDK startup. CG-07 integrates those production paths after its snapshot, archive and effect dependencies.
